lessons: Drift type B confirmed: Bot API had moved 10.2 (July 14, 2026) -> 10.3 (August 24, 2026). Nothing in 10.3 touches business accounts, payments, Stars or rate limits, so only the version reference needed changing.

BUG fixed: the skill asserted getUpdates returns 409 Conflict when a webhook is set, citing the API docs. Verified directly: the string 'Conflict' appears zero times on core.telegram.org/bots/api and every '409' hit is '4096 characters'. Telegram documents only the behavioural rule. Reframed 409 as observed symptom.

CRITICAL fixed (expert catch): the 409 row described the concurrent-polling scenario ('same token on a second platform') but prescribed deleteWebhook, which does nothing in that case. Split into the two real causes with the deleteWebhook-returns-true-and-nothing-changes tell.

BUG fixed: the skill said Israeli soleks are 'NOT on Telegram's officially-supported provider list'. There is no such list. The payments page says only 'more than 20 providers' and the real set is whatever @BotFather offers. Reframed.
Precision fix: 'features free to Premium subscribers' blurred two different things. The native Business features need the subscription; connected bots are explicitly available to non-Premium users.
Naming drift: the BotFather business toggle is 'Secretary Mode' on /bots/features and still 'Business Mode' on /bots. Both names documented so a reader finds either.
Added: deep-link payload cap (64 chars, A-Z a-z 0-9 _ -), the /start bizChat<user_chat_id> manage deep link, and the Stars obligations (XTR, mandatory /paysupport, provider_token physical-only).

CRITICAL fixed (expert catch): the word-cap restructuring moved the broadcast templates into a reference file as bare prose, stripping the פרסומת label, sender identification and opt-out, and left a 'see the spam-law section below' pointer to a section that did not exist there. An agent following that pointer would have written an s.30a-breaching promotion. Rebuilt as a real compliant template. Lesson: when a move is forced by the word cap, re-read the DESTINATION, not just the pointer.

Regression from the same restructuring: the two new reference files were not added to Bundled Resources in either language, and the Hebrew Reference Links table still advertised a Telegram 'provider list' that the same cycle had just established does not exist. Both fixed. Checklist row 13 now covers reference-file integrity.

CRITICAL fixed (expert catch): Chol HaMoed and erev chag were absent from the day model, so a booking bot built to spec sold full slots across roughly 10 holiday days a year. Added as owner-configurable short days, plus Yom HaZikaron.

CRITICAL fixed (expert catch): the חשבוניות ישראל allocation-number instruction omitted its scope. It applies to tax invoices issued to business customers deducting input VAT, so the cafes and salons this skill targets almost never hit it. As written it would have alarmed exactly the wrong audience. No figure is now quoted, since it changes annually.

Unsourced claims removed rather than asserted: 'Amendment 40 / 2008' for s.30a (the nevo text shows amendments 63/2016 and 72/2018 on the operative subsections), the four-item list of what Amendment 13 changed, 'Telegram crossed 1 billion MAU', Tranzila's 'since 1999' and 'API v2' version pin, and a stale NIS 190 donation-receipt threshold in the templates file.

BUG fixed (judge catch, second round): the skill told a business owner whose token leaked to send BotFather `/revoke`. Verified directly against core.telegram.org/bots/features: `/revoke` appears zero times and the documented remediation is `/token` ('If your existing token is compromised or you lost it for some reason, use the /token command to generate a new one'). The incident-response path in the skill did not work. Corrected in four places across both languages. Note the near-miss: the first repair split the evidence entry and gave it the snippet '/newbot', which is literally present on the page, so a snippet-appears-in-source check would have PASSED an entry whose claim was half false. A snippet must support the whole claim.

Legal gate false positive worth remembering: the Hebrew phrase 'התיעוד מנסח את זה' tripped verify_legal.py's document-DRAFTING signal and flipped the skill from clear to regulated. The word מנסח is the trigger. Reworded to מתאר rather than adding a spurious legal notice or an allowlist entry.

Verified correct, no change: ILS min 3.68 / max 36,788.20 (currencies.json exp=2), all six rate limits, Bot API 7.2 for connected bots, business_message / edited_business_message / business_connection_id, privacy mode and /setprivacy, Israel-vs-diaspora festival day-counts, the Hebcal i=on flag, and that nevo.co.il/law_html/law01/032_002.htm really is the Communications Law (a URL class that has served unrelated regulations before).

Deferred (expert MAJOR, over the batch-mode discretionary cap): direct marketing under Privacy Protection Law ss.17ג-17ו, which is a regime independent of s.30a; data-subject deletion routes built into the bot plus the Data Security Regulations tier; non-Jewish calendars (Friday-closed, Ramadan, Eid, Christmas) where the Sunday-Thursday assumption is currently hardcoded into booking logic; Cardcom in the provider table; sourcing for each provider row's invoice/API claims; first-instance case law applying s.30a to WhatsApp broadcasts.

Deferred (expert MINOR): the 'bot blocked' troubleshooting row omits the observable signal (HTTP 403 'Forbidden: bot was blocked by the user'); the Stars mobile-visibility claim is phrased harder than the source; small EN/HE drifts from editing the two files independently.

Structural note for next cycle: SKILL.md sits within a few dozen words of the 5,000-word body cap after seven sections were moved to references. Measure with the category validator before adding anything, and budget a matching removal. The Hebrew file has more headroom.
